title: Saltimbocca alla romana
intro: Veal, prosciutto and sage in a quick butter and white wine pan sauce.

steps.t: Pound the escalopes between two sheets of baking paper until thin and even.
Top each with a slice of prosciutto and a sage leaf; pin them with a toothpick.
Lightly flour only the side without prosciutto and shake off the excess.
Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat until it foams.
Cook meat side down for 2 minutes, until golden.
steps.label: Meat side

steps.t: Flip and cook 1 minute on the prosciutto side, until the veal is no longer pink.
steps.label: Ham side

steps.t: Pour in the wine and reduce for 2 minutes until syrupy. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Reduce

steps.t: Remove the toothpicks and serve at once with the pan juices.

tips.t: Go easy on the salt: the prosciutto is salty and the sauce concentrates as it reduces.
Serve with garlicky sautéed spinach or chicory.

title: Ossobuco alla milanese
intro: Veal shanks braised slowly until falling off the bone, finished with gremolata.

steps.t: Snip the membrane around each shank in 3-4 places so they don't curl as they cook.
Flour, salt and brown them in butter in a wide pan, 4 minutes per side, until golden.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Lift out the meat, add the chopped onion, carrot and celery and cook over medium heat until soft.
steps.label: Soffritto

steps.t: Return the shanks, pour in the wine and let it bubble away.
steps.label: Deglaze

steps.t: Add hot stock (store-bought is fine) halfway up the meat, cover and simmer gently.
steps.label: Braise

pressure.t: Pressure cooker: add stock halfway up, lock the lid and cook 35 minutes at high pressure over low heat.

steps.t: Turn the shanks, add more stock if needed and cook until the meat comes away from the bone.
steps.label: Braise 2

pressure.t: Release the pressure, turn the shanks and, if the sauce is thin, reduce it uncovered for 5 minutes.

steps.t: Meanwhile, make the gremolata: finely chop the lemon zest, garlic and parsley together.
Scatter the gremolata over the shanks, cover and rest off the heat before serving.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: The classic partner is saffron risotto alla milanese.
Don't waste the marrow: spread it on toast or stir it into the risotto.
Even better the next day: reheat gently with a splash of stock.

title: Chicken cacciatore
intro: Chicken braised with tomato, red wine, rosemary and olives in a rich sauce.

steps.t: Pat the chicken dry, salt it and brown it in the oil in a wide casserole until golden all over.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Lift out the chicken, lower the heat and fry the sliced onion, garlic and rosemary until the onion is soft.
steps.label: Soffritto

steps.t: Return the chicken, pour in the red wine and let it bubble away.
steps.label: Deglaze

steps.t: Add the crushed tomatoes and a pinch of salt, cover and cook over low heat, turning halfway.
steps.label: Braise

oven.t: Add the tomatoes and salt, cover and bake at 170°C for 45 minutes, turning the chicken halfway.

steps.t: Stir in the olives and cook uncovered until the sauce thickens.
steps.label: Thicken

steps.t: Check it's done: the chicken should read 75°C near the bone and the juices should run clear.
Remove the rosemary, adjust the seasoning and serve with soft polenta.

tips.t: With soft polenta it's a Sunday lunch classic across central Italy.
Add 300 g button mushrooms with the olives for an autumn version.

title: Cotoletta alla milanese
intro: Bone-in veal chop, double-breaded and fried in clarified butter.

steps.t: Gently pound the meat around the bone, without detaching it, until about 1.5 cm thick.
Beat the eggs in a shallow dish and tip the breadcrumbs into another.
Dip the chops in egg, then in breadcrumbs, pressing well; repeat for a double coating.
Heat the clarified butter in a large frying pan over medium heat until it just sizzles, about 160°C.

airfryer.t: Brush both sides of the chops with melted clarified butter and preheat the air fryer to 200°C.

steps.t: Fry the first side until the crumb is hazelnut brown.
steps.label: First side

airfryer.t: Cook in the basket at 200°C for 8 minutes, without overlapping.

steps.t: Turn with a spatula and fry the other side: the meat should reach at least 63°C in the centre.
steps.label: Second side

airfryer.t: Turn and cook 6 more minutes, until golden and at least 63°C in the centre.

steps.t: Drain on kitchen paper, salt and serve straight away with lemon wedges.

tips.t: Don't detach the meat from the bone when pounding: the bone keeps it juicy.
Pounded very thin without the bone, it becomes the 'elephant ear', crisp edge to edge.
Serve with rocket and cherry tomatoes dressed with olive oil and lemon.

title: Meatballs in tomato sauce
intro: Tender meatballs simmered slowly in tomato sauce, Italian Sunday style.

steps.t: Soak the bread in the milk, then squeeze it out well.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: Mix the meat, bread, egg, Parmigiano, parsley, salt and pepper until evenly combined.
With wet hands, shape about 20 walnut-sized meatballs.
In a wide pan, bring the tomato sauce (a good jarred one works) and the water to a simmer.
Lay the raw meatballs in the sauce without stirring, cover and cook over low heat.
steps.label: Meatballs

steps.t: Turn them gently and cook uncovered until the sauce is thick.
steps.label: Thicken

steps.t: Break one open: it must not be pink inside (72°C in the centre). Add basil and serve.

tips.t: Milk-soaked bread, not dry breadcrumbs, is what keeps them soft.
They keep 2 days in the fridge in their sauce; leftover sauce makes the next day's pasta.
Add 150 g peas for the last 10 minutes for a heartier version.

title: Chicken tikka masala
intro: Yogurt-marinated chicken, charred, in a creamy spiced tomato sauce.

steps.t: Cut the chicken into 3 cm cubes and mix with yogurt, lemon, 1 tsp garam masala, turmeric, chilli and salt.
Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: Spread the chicken on a lined tray and cook under the grill at 250°C until charred at the edges.
steps.label: Grill

airfryer.t: Cook the chicken in the air fryer at 200°C for 12 minutes, shaking the basket halfway.

bbq.t: Thread the chicken on skewers and cook over direct heat on the barbecue for 10 minutes, turning often.

steps.t: Meanwhile, fry the chopped onions in the oil over medium heat until golden.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Add grated garlic and ginger and the rest of the garam masala; stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the passata and cook until thick, with the oil pooling at the edges.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Blend the sauce if you like it smooth, then add the cream and the chicken with its juices.
Simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through: 75°C in the centre, no pink inside.
steps.label: Chicken

steps.t: Scatter with coriander and serve with basmati rice or naan.

tips.t: The charred bits on the chicken give the sauce its smoky depth, so don't skip the grill.
A teaspoon of dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi) at the end makes it taste authentic.
Serve with basmati rice and a cucumber raita.

title: Beef bulgogi
intro: Korean beef marinated with pear, soy and sesame, caramelised over high heat.

steps.t: Grate the pear, garlic and ginger and mix with the soy, sugar, sesame oil and pepper.
Add the beef, sliced onion and half the sliced spring onions; massage well with your hands.
Cover and marinate in the fridge.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: Heat a cast-iron pan with the oil over high heat until just smoking.
Cook the beef in small batches, 2-3 minutes each, until caramelised and no longer pink.
steps.label: Pan

bbq.t: On the barbecue use a fine grill mat: cook over direct heat 2 minutes per batch, turning once.

steps.t: Scatter with the remaining spring onions and sesame; serve with rice and lettuce leaves.

tips.t: If the beef isn't pre-sliced, freeze it for 30 minutes so you can slice it paper-thin.
Wrap it in lettuce leaves with rice and kimchi, Seoul style.

title: Lemon and thyme roast chicken
intro: Crisp skin, juicy meat and potatoes roasted in the pan juices.

steps.t: Take the chicken out of the fridge and pat it very dry inside and out with kitchen paper.
steps.label: Room temp

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C. Cut the potatoes into wedges and toss them in the tin with 1 tbsp oil, salt and half the thyme.
Stuff the chicken with the pricked lemon, 3 garlic cloves and the rest of the thyme; tie the legs with string.
Rub the skin with the remaining oil, salt and pepper; sit it on the potatoes with the rest of the garlic and the water.
Roast at 220°C until the skin starts to colour.
steps.label: High heat

steps.t: Lower to 190°C and roast, basting halfway, until the thigh reads 75°C and the juices run clear.
steps.label: Roast

steps.t: Tent the chicken with foil and let it rest; meanwhile return the potatoes to the oven if you want them crisper.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Carve the chicken and serve with the potatoes and pan juices.

tips.t: Salt the chicken the night before and leave it uncovered in the fridge for super-crisp skin.
Use the carcass and scraps to make chicken stock for the next day.
Swap the lemon for an orange and add a few sprigs of rosemary.

title: Lamb tagine with apricots
intro: Spiced lamb slowly cooked with apricots and honey, sweet and savoury.

steps.t: Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy casserole over medium-high heat, in batches, until golden.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Add the chopped onions and garlic and cook until soft.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Stir in the ginger, cinnamon, cumin, saffron, salt and pepper for 1 minute.
Pour in the water, bring to the boil, cover and simmer gently until the meat is tender.
steps.label: Stew

pressure.t: Pressure cooker: add the water, lock the lid and cook 35 minutes at high pressure, then release.

steps.t: Add the apricots and honey and cook uncovered until the sauce is thick and glossy.
steps.label: Apricots

steps.t: Meanwhile, toast the almonds in a dry frying pan until golden.
Serve topped with the almonds and coriander, with couscous or flatbread.

tips.t: Serve with steamed couscous dressed with a little olive oil and salt.
A teaspoon of ras el hanout instead of the single spices makes it more fragrant.
Even better the next day; it freezes well for up to 3 months.

title: Pork souvlaki with tzatziki
intro: Greek skewers marinated in lemon and oregano, with fresh tzatziki and pita.

steps.t: Cut the pork into 3 cm cubes and mix with 4 tbsp oil, lemon, oregano, 2 crushed garlic cloves, salt and pepper.
Cover and marinate in the fridge; soak the skewers in water.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: Meanwhile, make the tzatziki: grate the cucumber, salt it, squeeze it dry, then mix with yogurt, garlic, dill and 1 tbsp oil.
Thread the meat onto the skewers and heat a griddle pan over high heat.
Cook the skewers, turning often, until browned and the pork reaches 70°C in the centre.
steps.label: Cook

bbq.t: Cook over medium-high direct heat on the barbecue for 10 minutes, turning often, until the pork reaches 70°C.

airfryer.t: Air-fry at 200°C for 14 minutes, turning halfway, until the pork reaches 70°C.

steps.t: Warm the pitas on the griddle, 30 seconds per side.

airfryer.t: Warm the pitas in a dry frying pan, 30 seconds per side.

steps.t: Serve the skewers on the pitas with tomatoes, sliced red onion and tzatziki.

tips.t: Squeeze the cucumber hard: any water left makes the tzatziki runny.
Use boneless chicken thighs instead of pork and cook them to 75°C in the centre.
